summary: A stone draw-well: three courses of dressed blocks under a coping ring, two posts, a shingled gable roof, a cranked windlass with coiled rope and a hanging bucket.
objective: At three metres the well reads as a roof over a round drum, then block courses, shingle courses and the crank, then rope coils, iron bands and hue jitter.
intent_signals: add a well to a village square
example_prompts: Put a well in the middle of the village square.
I need a wellhead with a working-looking crank and bucket.
not_for: Any claim about well construction, depth or water safety.
A mechanism: the crank and windlass do not turn and the rope does not spool.

silhouette: a shingled gable 2.7 m up over a 1.32 m round stone drum
two posts carrying the roof clear of the well mouth
a bucket hanging over the mouth on its rope, clear of the coping
medium: three courses of twelve dressed blocks, each course offset half a block
a coping ring of twelve cap stones overhanging the drum by 3.7 cm
shingle courses laid five to the metre of slope, each lapping the one below
a cranked arm and handle standing off the end of the windlass
two posts rising to the ridge beam with a rafter from the ridge to each eave over every post, so the roof is carried rather than floating
fine: five rope coils wound over the windlass barrel, each 2.8 cm thick
two iron bands on the windlass ends and an iron hoop around the bucket
1.8 cm chamfer on the blocks and 1.6 cm on the coping
per-block hue jitter of 7 percent across the thirty-six drum blocks

principles: Offsetting every other course by half a block is what turns a ring of identical boxes into masonry; without it the drum reads as an extruded circle.
The roof is the silhouette and the crank is the story. Both have to survive the far view or the well reads as a stone tube.
The bucket hanging in the mouth is the cheapest way to say the well is in use.
implementation: Call create({ radius, postHeight, seed, blocks, wall, drumHeight, roofPitchDeg }); the group is centred on the drum with y = 0 at the ground.
Set a figure at the crank socket or a pail on the rim socket; both are placed on real geometry, not on a bounding box.
Drum blocks, coping and shingles are five instanced fields, so the well costs about a dozen draw calls.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
The crank socket sits out past the post line: its x is greater than 0.3.
Two seeds differ visibly in block tone while keeping the same course offsets.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real well or its construction.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters; twenty blocks a course costs about 3800 triangles.
Nothing turns: the crank, windlass and rope are static geometry, and the bucket hangs at a fixed depth.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Drop the roof pitch and widen the radius for a village cistern, or re-colour the blocks dark and the shingles slate for a hill village.

defaults.rationale: A 79 cm coping is hip height on a 1.7 m figure, the height at which leaning over the rim reads as safe, and a 38 degree pitch keeps the roof from hiding the crank.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds: the drum footprint and the roof ridge.

T2.note: Six families are mapped: posts, windlass and bucket take wood, the little roof takes roof-tile, the windlass ironwork takes metal, the rope takes fabric, the drum block courses and the coping take stone. The blocks were left flat at revision 3 because repeatFor misjudged a 0.31 m extruded block as normalised UVs and magnified one ashlar 2.6x; kit-surface now keys ExtrudeGeometry by type, so revision 4 maps them.

T3.note: No baked glTF ships for this blueprint: phase 9C baked only the two heroes (timber-cottage and watermill).

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
